newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian premier to address Duma on budget.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier to address Duma on budget.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will address the lower house of parliament on April 23 and outline the government's ability to meet 1997 budget plans, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.
Tass, quoting Duma speaker Gennady Seleznyov, said the discussions would deal with the budget in the first quarter -- three months marked by sharply lower than forecast revenues.
Under the Russian budget law, the government must ask parliament to approve new spending proposals if revenues are more than 10 percent below planned levels over a quarter.
Parliament may then seek a say in what is cut and what is protected from across-the-board sequestration.

This throws up the prospect of a lingering row between the conservative legislature and reformist ministers appointed last month. The Duma, elected in December 1995 is dominated by communists and their conservatives allies, while the latest changes have given the government a more reformist bent.

Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh, a new appointee as a deputy premier and minister responsible for privatisation, said this weekend that first quarter tax collection was 58 percent of budgeted levels. He called it "a crisis of statehood".
